stem: A committee of 3 members is selected at random from a group of 5 men and 3 women. What is the probability that the committee contains exactly 2 women?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Mistakenly computes C(3,2) = 3 as the only favourable case (forgets to multiply by C(5,1) = 5 for the one man), giving 3/56.
Uses C(8,2) = 28 as the denominator (choosing 2 from 8) instead of C(8,3) = 56 for a committee of 3, giving 15/28.
Computes C(5,1)/C(8,3) = 5/56 then miscopies as 5/28, confusing the number of men selected with the favourable count.

explanation: Exactly 2 women and 1 man: choose 2 from 3 women = C(3,2) = 3; choose 1 from 5 men = C(5,1) = 5. Combined favourable = 3 x 5 = 15. Total ways to choose any 3 from 8 = C(8,3) = 56. P = 15/56.

explanation_sections.punchline: Break by gender: C(3,2) x C(5,1) = 15 favourable out of C(8,3) = 56 total gives 15/56.
explanation_sections.approach: Classical probability with combinations. Decompose the favourable event by gender slot: (ways to pick 2 women from 3) x (ways to pick 1 man from 5). Then divide by total ways to form the committee. This multiplicative decomposition is the core move for mixed-composition problems.
explanation_sections.lesson: For exact-composition problems, multiply the sub-group combination counts and divide by the total group combination count.
explanation_sections.timing: 40 seconds. C(8,3) = 56 is a standard value to know. Spot the missing-multiplication trap (option 2).
